As the tide falls, exposing trapped crustaceans and fi sh within tidal pools, the cerrophol stalks out of the surf to survey the pickings. 
Th ough resembling an octopus, this semi-terrestrial squid uses its two feeding tentacles to hunt above the waves. Th rough the selective 
pressures of evolution, they have hardened into claw-like tips for dragging its body across stone and sand, as well as cracking urchin 
and crab shell that it hunts for with its forward facing predatory eyes. With enough salt water held in its mantle for short trips upon the 
sand, the creature can make use of the often trapped prey in this alternating environment. Unfortunately for this squid, many other 
predators along Sol’Kesh coasts have adapted to this same tidal ecosystem strategy, and the competition to thrive is fi erce.

Coastal Hunter Th e cerrophol can breathe only water, and while 
out of water, it can hold its breath for 1 hour.
Polarized Sight Th e cerrophol has Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) 
checks to determine if a creature is being deceptive about its 
appearance, whether through magical or mundane means.
Twisting Form Th e cerrophol writing tentacles makes the squid 
diffi cult to grasp, it has Advantage on Saving Th rows made to 
escape the Grappled condition.

Piercing Tentacle - 18 gp
DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) Check

Calamari Ring - 1 gp

Encountering Naturally inquisitive, the cerrophol has adapted 
to a life of changing tides and is quick to react to new creatures. 
If a Traveler acts as if they have no interest in eating it, the squid 
may follow them stealthily, attempting to sate its curiosity. A 
traveler that drops miscellaneous items, each more unique than 
the last, will eventually convince the squid to approach, its sense 
of self-preservation forgotten by its own sense of wonder.
Multiattack Th e cerrophol makes two attacks, using Piercing 
Tentacles and Gripping Arms in any combination.
Piercing Tentacles Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one 
target. Hit: 12 (2d8+3) Piercing damage. Until the start of the 
cerrophol’s next turn, attack rolls made against the same target 
creature are made with Advantage.
Gripping Arms Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one 
target. Hit: 6 (1d6+3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a 
Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition 
(Escape DC 15) from one of its eight arms.
Ink Spill (1/Day) Trigger: Th e cerrophol takes damage while out 
of the water. Response: It releases a 15 ft. radius puddle of slippery 
ink centered on its body. Th e area becomes diffi cult terrain for 1 
minute. Any creature that moves on the ink must make a DC 14 
Dexterity Saving Th row or get the Prone condition. Th e ink can 
be washed away with at least 2 gallons of water.
Aggressive Instinct (1/Day) When Bloodied and engaged in melee 
combat, the cerrophol begins to flail wildly.
On its turn, Wisdom Saving Th row: DC 12, the cerrophol. Success: Th e 
cerrophol gains a third attack for its Multiattack action. Failure: 
Th e cerrophol is overcome with fear and makes a free Disengage 
and Dash action in any direction away from adversaries. 
Speed 20 ft., swim 40 ft.
Thick razor edged chitin encases 
the tip of the tentacle, allowing the 
cerrophol to pierce and crack its prey
The cephalopod’s golden eyes perceive colors to 
pursue prey by the use of chromatic aberration. 
Through monitoring blurriness during focus changes 
they can make out variations of hues across the 
vibrant tidal pools 
A hardened mantle protects the squid 
from coastal predators and retains 
water 
for

become smooth and toughened. While lacking
